newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl remains commited to timely euro launch -govt.
newsitem.headline: Kohl remains commited to timely euro launch -govt.

text.p: A German government spokesman said on Monday Chancellor Helmut Kohl remained commited to a timely launch of Europe's single currency even though Kohl had stressed on Sunday that the stability of the euro was his top priority.

"The chancellor said quite clearly that there would be no weak euro," government spokesman Herbert Schmuelling told reporters. "The schedule and the criteria remain valid as they were in the past. There has been no change in the mood."

In an interview with ZDF television on Sunday evening from his holiday in the Austrian alps, Kohl said that even though he was commited to European integration he would not sacrifice monetary stability. He said he would not accept a weak euro.
"Whoever believes that Helmut Kohl will give up the policy (of stability) out of enthusiasm for Europe and day-to-day factors... is wrong. That is a price I will not pay."

Bavarian state premier Edmund Stoiber has in several recent newspaper interviews said the euro launch should be put back if countries overshoot the Maastricht budget deficit goal of three percent of gross domestic product.

Kohl has bowed to pressure from Stoiber and pledged to meet the strict 3.0 deficit percent interpretation of the budget deficit criteria to allay fears of those who believe a fudged currency union would result in a soft euro.
